title: A nontrivial homogeneous invertible module on an abelian variety is coherently acyclic
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $P$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $a\in A(k)$ let $t_a:A\to A$ be the translation $x\mapsto x+a$, and let $t_a^*$ be tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume $t_a^*P\cong P$ for every $a\in A(k)$ and $P\not\cong\mathcal O_A$. Then $H^i(A,P)=0$ for every integer $i\geq0$, where $H^i$ is coherent Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. There is no restriction on the characteristic of $k$ or the dimension of $A$; algebraic triviality is not a hypothesis.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 8.4(b),(c), printed pp.35–36 (homogeneous-to-multiplicative equivalence), and Corollary 5.18, printed p.26 (seesaw). The acyclicity consequence is an agent-supplied supporting lemma for the proof of Proposition 8.14; it is not asserted to be the statement printed in those places.

proof.text: Write $e\in A(k)$ for the identity, $a:A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure map, and $p_1,p_2:A\times_kA\to A$ for the projections. By [def-sc-abelian-variety], $A$ is proper, smooth and connected. By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] it is geometrically integral. Thus [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety](2) gives $\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)=k$ through the structure homomorphism. In particular every nonzero constant global function is a unit. The rational identity ensures nonemptiness; these assertions also apply when $\dim A=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BUG, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections (8); groupoid.tex Tags 0B7Q and 0BFC, geometric integrality of an abelian variety.

proof.text: Let $m(x,y)=x+y$ and put $N=m^*P\otimes(p_1^*P)^\vee\otimes(p_2^*P)^\vee$. Pullbacks are the tensor pullbacks of [def-pc-module-pullback]; they commute with tensor products by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. They also commute with duals of invertible modules: for a morphism $g$ and an invertible $\mathcal L$, $g^*\mathcal O=\mathcal O$ by the formula for $g^*$, so $g^*(\mathcal L^\vee)\otimes g^*\mathcal L\cong g^*(\mathcal L^\vee\otimes\mathcal L)\cong\mathcal O$, and tensoring with $(g^*\mathcal L)^\vee$ and using the evaluation isomorphisms of [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible] gives $g^*(\mathcal L^\vee)\cong(g^*\mathcal L)^\vee$. These two rules, with the composition clause of [def-pc-module-pullback], compute every restriction below. By [def-sc-invertible-module] and [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible], $N$ is invertible. Choose a basis of the one-dimensional fibre $P_e$. For each $y\in A(k)$, the restriction of $N$ to $A\times\{y\}$ is $t_y^*P\otimes P^\vee\otimes_k P_y^\vee$, which is trivial: use the given translation isomorphism, evaluation $P\otimes P^\vee\cong\mathcal O_A$, and a basis of $P_y$. The restriction to $\{e\}\times A$ is $P\otimes_kP_e^\vee\otimes P^\vee$, also trivial. Apply [lem-sfb-rigidified-product-seesaw] to $V=T=A$, $x=e$, and $\mathcal H=N$. Step 1 verifies proper geometric integrality of $V$; $T$ is smooth, separated and of finite type since $A$ is an abelian variety. Its conclusion $N\cong p_2^*e^*N$ and the identity-axis trivialization give $N\cong\mathcal O_{A\times A}$. Tensor with $p_1^*P\otimes p_2^*P$ and cancel dual pairs, obtaining $m^*P\cong p_1^*P\otimes p_2^*P$. No algebraic-equivalence assertion is used.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4(b) implies (c), printed pp.35–36, using Corollary 5.18, printed p.26; fibre and identity-axis cancellations made explicit.

proof.text: Fix $i\geq0$ and set $V=H^i(A,P)$ in the cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology]. The line module $P$ is quasi-coherent and finitely presented, being locally free of rank one. By [lem-fin-proper-coherent-finite-dimensional], $V$ has finite dimension $n$ over $k$. The map $a$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field] and is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by properness. Apply the sheaf form of [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to the base change of $a$ by itself, with coefficient $P$: $R^ip_{2*}p_1^*P\cong V\otimes_k\mathcal O_A$. Here a module sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is its vector space of sections. Set $\sigma(x,y)=(x+y,y)$; its inverse is $(z,y)\mapsto(z-y,y)$, and $p_2\sigma=p_2$, $p_1\sigma=m$. Pullback by this isomorphism is an exact equivalence, with inverse pullback by $\sigma^{-1}$, so it preserves injective resolutions. Applying $p_{2*}$ to a pulled-back resolution gives the original direct image, using $p_2\sigma^{-1}=p_2$. Hence $R^ip_{2*}m^*P\cong R^ip_{2*}p_1^*P$. By Step 2 and [lem-pc-projection-formula] for the invertible factor $P$, its left side is also $(R^ip_{2*}p_1^*P)\otimes P$. Taking degree $i$ in that derived formula is legitimate since tensoring with $P$ is exact: locally it is tensoring with $\mathcal O_A$. We obtain $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_A\cong V\otimes_kP$, and a basis of $V$ gives $\mathcal O_A^{\oplus n}\cong P^{\oplus n}$.

source.place: Tags 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology) and 02O6 (lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite); cohomology.tex Tag 01E8 (lemma-projection-formula). The addition shear and its inverse are the explicit agent assembly.

proof.text: If $V\neq0$, then $n>0$. Write the isomorphism of Step 3 as $u:P^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal O_A^{\oplus n}$ with inverse $v$. The $(1,1)$ entry of $uv=1$ says $\sum_{j=1}^n u_{1j}v_{j1}=1$ in $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal O_A)=\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)=k$. Thus some $c=u_{1j}v_{j1}$ is a nonzero element of $k$. The maps $s=v_{j1}:\mathcal O_A\to P$ and $t=c^{-1}u_{1j}:P\to\mathcal O_A$ satisfy $ts=1$. On each open trivializing $P$, these maps are multiplication by functions $f,g$ with $gf=1$. Since the local rings are commutative, also $fg=1$, so $s$ is an isomorphism there; the local inverses are the restrictions of $t$, giving $P\cong\mathcal O_A$ globally. This contradicts the hypothesis. Consequently $V=0$. Since $i\geq0$ was arbitrary, every required cohomology group vanishes. The argument divides only by the nonzero scalar $c$, never by $n$.
